app.name: SoloStudio
app.summary: SoloStudio is for a solo freelance UX designer whose clients, notes, tasks and bookings are currently scattered across email, notes and spreadsheets. It brings clients, follow-up notes, projects and tasks, availability and public bookings into one private workspace. The designer tracks follow-ups and work from a home dashboard, while visitors book an available session from her public booking page.
app.audience: A solo freelance UX designer managing her own clients, projects and bookings, and the people who book sessions with her without an account.

roles.name: Designer
roles.description: The solo freelance UX designer who owns the workspace and manages clients, projects, tasks, availability and sessions.

roles.name: Booking guest
roles.description: A person booking a session who never signs in and uses the public booking page and a cancellation link.

vocabulary.description: A person or company the designer works with: name, email, optional company, short profile and status Lead, Active or Past.
A dated note under a Client from a call, with an optional follow-up date that can be marked done or pushed a week.
Work for a Client with a name, short description and optional due date, holding Tasks.
A task in a Project with a title, status To do, In progress or Done, priority Low, Medium or High and an optional due date.
The designer's weekly availability: which days and from what time to what time she can be booked.
A kind of bookable session with duration, displayed price and maximum people, such as a discovery call, design review or Figma workshop.
A bookable time for a SessionType generated from Availability, full when its Bookings reach the SessionType maximum; cancelling it cancels all its Bookings.
One person's place on a Slot, made with name and email, linked to a Client by matching email or creating a Lead, cancellable via its on-screen link.

inScope: Public landing page that explains SoloStudio is a single workspace for a solo freelance designer to manage clients, projects and bookings, with sign-up and sign-in for the designer and a link to her public booking page.
The designer signs up and signs in to a private workspace that only she can access; all Clients, Notes, Projects, Tasks, Availability, SessionTypes, Slots and Bookings belong to her.
Clients with name, email, optional company, a short profile (what they do, how we met, what they pay) and a status of Lead, Active or Past; the designer can create, view, edit and delete a Client.
Dated Notes jotted under each Client after calls, each with an optional follow-up date; the designer can add, edit and delete Notes.

Client list sorted so overdue follow-ups come first, then follow-ups due soonest, showing who is due for a follow-up; from the list the designer can mark a follow-up done or push it a week with one click.
Projects that belong to a Client, with a name, a short description and an optional due date; the designer can create, view, edit and delete a Project.
Tasks under a Project with a title, a status (To do, In progress, Done), a priority (Low, Medium, High) and an optional due date; the designer can create, edit, delete and tick a Task done quickly.

A projects view showing all Projects with how many Tasks are still open; opening a Project shows its Tasks, which can be filtered by status and priority and searched by title, with overdue Tasks standing out.
Deleting a Project deletes its Tasks, and deleting a Client deletes its Projects, Tasks and Notes.

The designer sets weekly Availability (which days, from what time to what time) and defines SessionTypes with duration, displayed price and maximum people: a 30 minute discovery call (free, 1 person), a 60 minute design review (₹4,000 shown for information, 1 person) and a 2 hour Figma workshop (₹2,500 a seat, up to 8 people). Prices are only displayed; nobody pays in the app.

Public booking page with no account needed: a visitor picks a SessionType, sees open Slots for the next two weeks, and books with only their name and email, then sees a confirmation and their cancellation link on screen; no emails are sent.

A Slot is full when its Bookings reach the SessionType maximum and is then no longer offered; if a booking email matches a Client, the Booking lands under that Client, otherwise a new Client is created as a Lead.
A visitor can cancel their own Booking using the cancellation link shown after booking, which frees their seat.
The designer sees upcoming sessions (Slots with their Bookings) and can cancel a Slot, which cancels everyone booked on it.
Home screen for the designer showing today's sessions, follow-ups due this week and overdue Tasks, each linking to the relevant Client, session or Project.

outOfScope.item: Taking payment for paid session types
outOfScope.reason: The idea states prices are only displayed and nobody pays in the app.
outOfScope.placeholder: Prices are displayed as information only on the SessionType and booking page, and a Booking is confirmed without payment.

outOfScope.item: Email confirmations, reminders or cancellation emails
outOfScope.reason: The idea states no emails are sent and the cancellation link is shown on screen.
outOfScope.placeholder: The booking confirmation and cancellation link are shown on screen immediately after booking, and the designer checks upcoming sessions in the app.

outOfScope.item: Accounts or a portal for clients and people booking
outOfScope.reason: The idea states people booking don't have accounts and the app is just for the designer.
outOfScope.placeholder: Visitors book and cancel through the public booking page and their on-screen cancellation link without signing in.

outOfScope.item: Team members, shared workspaces or other freelancers
outOfScope.reason: The idea asks for one app just for her.
outOfScope.placeholder: The workspace is private to the single designer who signed up.

outOfScope.item: Calendar sync, video-call links and invoicing
outOfScope.reason: Not asked for in the idea; the profile records what clients pay as free text.
outOfScope.placeholder: Sessions, client payment notes in the profile and tasks are tracked inside SoloStudio only.

assumptions.text: A Client requires only name and email; company and profile are optional, and status defaults to Lead unless the designer changes it.

Marking a follow-up done clears its follow-up date; pushing it a week adds 7 days to the current follow-up date. A follow-up is overdue when its date is before today and it is not marked done, and due this week when its date falls within the current calendar week.
An open Task is any task whose status is not Done. A Task is overdue when it has a due date before today and is not Done.

The three session types named in the idea are pre-created for the designer (30 minute discovery call, free, maximum 1; 60 minute design review, ₹4,000 displayed, maximum 1; 2 hour Figma workshop, ₹2,500 a seat displayed, maximum 8) and the designer can edit them and her weekly Availability.

Open Slots are generated from the designer's weekly Availability in her own time zone for the next 14 days, long enough for the chosen SessionType, and a Slot that already holds a Booking does not accept an overlapping Booking for a different session type.

The cancellation link shown after booking is a unique private link for that Booking; using it cancels only that person's Booking and frees their seat, while cancelling a Slot as the designer cancels every Booking on it.

Client matching on booking is by exact email address, case-insensitive. Deleting a Client deletes its Notes, Projects and their Tasks as stated, and leaves its Bookings visible in the session list without a client link.
Changing Availability or a SessionType affects Slots offered afterwards and does not move or cancel Bookings already made.

questions.question: When different session types share the same availability, can they be booked at overlapping times?
questions.whyItMatters: This changes when a Slot counts as open or full and whether the designer can be double-booked.
questions.defaultAnswer: A booked time blocks overlapping Slots for every other session type, so the designer is never double-booked.

questions.question: Are the three session types fixed, or can the designer edit and add session types?
questions.whyItMatters: This changes whether SessionType is editable data or fixed configuration.
questions.defaultAnswer: The three named session types are pre-created and the designer can edit their duration, displayed price and maximum people, and add her own.

questions.question: When a Client with Bookings is deleted, should those Bookings also be deleted?
questions.whyItMatters: This changes what deleting a Client removes beyond the projects and notes the idea names.
questions.defaultAnswer: Bookings stay in the upcoming and past session list without a client link; the Client's Notes, Projects and Tasks are deleted.
